method: Read under subscription in the operator's browser and PARAPHRASED. No AMH passage reproduced and no source_text stored; every claim carries a locator and verdict licensed_source_not_quoted. Dose claims flagged dose:true. Ocular rosacea and the phymatous and erythematotelangiectatic subtypes are not covered by this topic and are recorded as out_of_scope rather than filled from elsewhere. The brimonidine monograph refers to its own Counselling section, which was not retrieved.

claims.claim: Rosacea is a chronic and relapsing inflammatory skin disorder characterised by central facial erythema, flushing and telangiectasia, with inflammatory papules and pustules sometimes present
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: The aim of rosacea treatment is to reduce the symptoms
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Antibiotics are used for their anti-inflammatory effects in papulopustular rosacea
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Topical metronidazole or azelaic acid is used for mild inflammatory papules or pustules, with metronidazole preferred because it is less irritating, and topical ivermectin as an alternative
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Improvement with topical treatment may occur after 2 to 4 weeks but full effect often takes 6 to 12 weeks, and long-term metronidazole treatment may be needed
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Oral antibacterials are used for moderate to severe inflammatory papules or pustules or when topical therapy is inadequate, with doxycycline the drug of choice and erythromycin an alternative if doxycycline is unsuccessful or contraindicated though evidence of erythromycin efficacy is limited
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: A 4 to 12 week course of oral antibacterial is often used and repeated as required, and in some cases long-term treatment is needed
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Combination oral doxycycline with topical metronidazole or azelaic acid has been used for more severe disease or inadequate topical therapy but evidence is limited
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Patients should be referred to a dermatologist if rosacea does not respond to or recurs after oral antibiotics or combination therapy, where other treatments such as isotretinoin may be suitable
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Topical brimonidine may be used for persistent facial erythema due to rosacea, applied daily as required
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Patients should minimise or avoid factors causing flushing or skin irritation including emotional stress, extremes of temperature, alcohol, hot drinks, spicy foods, sun or wind exposure and chemical exfoliating agents, and use a soap substitute with pH around 6
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Papulopustular rosacea often relapses after stopping isotretinoin and repeat courses or long-term treatment may be needed
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Specialists may continue isotretinoin for example for 4 to 8 weeks after inflammatory lesions are well controlled
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Rosacea' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for rosacea), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Topical metronidazole for rosacea is applied as a gel or cream rubbed as a thin film into affected areas twice a day
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Metronidazole (skin)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-rosacea/metronidazole-skin, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Azelaic acid is applied morning and night
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Azelaic acid' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-acne/other-drugs-acne/azelaic-acid, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Topical ivermectin for rosacea is applied once a day for up to 4 months with a repeat course if needed
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Ivermectin (skin)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-rosacea/ivermectin-skin, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Topical brimonidine is used once a day or less often, starting with a small amount of gel and increasing gradually after 1 week to no more than a small pea-sized amount to each area of the face
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Brimonidine (skin)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-rosacea/brimonidine-skin, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Doxycycline for rosacea is adult oral 50 mg once daily
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Doxycycline' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/antibacterials/tetracyclines/doxycycline, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Erythromycin for acne and rosacea is adult and child over 12 years oral 250 to 500 mg twice daily
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Erythromycin' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/anti-infectives/antibacterials/macrolides/erythromycin, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Isotretinoin for rosacea is a usual initial dose of 0.25 to 0.3 mg/kg daily in 1 or 2 doses adjusted to response and tolerance with a maximum of 1 mg/kg daily which may be poorly tolerated, using the lowest effective dose which may be very low such as 10 mg three times a week
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Isotretinoin' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-acne/retinoids-oral/isotretinoin, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
